a key-gated session mouth, closed by default.
# dsh-backroom
A read-only **back room** for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) plugin authors: it makes the host's own log b
uffer readable over loopback HTTP, and reports — live, in the running process — which official servi
ce faces a plugin can actually reach.
`dsh-backroom` is a community plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Not an official DeepSeek AI product.
## Why this plugin exists
Two things were missing on the installed desktop host (0.2.0-rc.2), and neither is an API gap:
- **Nobody reads the host's log buffer.** `ctx.logger`'s only built-in sink is cordis' in-memory rin
g (`logger.buffer`, 1000 entries), and the shipped product registers a second exporter only for the
fatal-startup path. Host code logs through `logger`, not `console` (`dsh-hmr` alone emits 19 logger
calls), and in the packaged app the backend child's stdout is piped into a GUI process and lost. So

"the plugin mounted but did nothing" had no evidence at all.
- **Reachability was measured once and
recorded wrong.** Whether `ctx.get('sessionController')` works from a plugin fiber is decided in the
running process, not in a `.d.ts` file. This plugin answers that with a live matrix instead of a gu
ning process, not in a `.d.ts` file. This plugin answers that with a live matrix instead of a guess.
## What it does
Current build (0.4 — the six pain points from the 2026-11-01 field session, turned into routes) is t
he **probe + fault-attribution + narrow session mouth + session-creation + declarations + per-plugin
hot-reload** shape: host half only, **eight** loopback routes (five read-only, three that act), no
UI. The plugin's only "write" is the `reload` route touching the target plugin's entry-file mtime (m
etadata only — see the reload row).
| Route | Returns |
| `GET /dsh-backroom/probe` | Per-service matrix: for each name, `ctx.get(name, true)` / `ctx.get(na
me, false)` reported separately as `present(<type>)` / `absent` / `threw: <message>`, plus the face'
s own method names; property-access results for declared vs undeclared deps; `hmr.getLinked()` as-is
; how many log records were already buffered before this plugin applied (that is the replayability r
eading); node/argv/`DSH_*` env **names**; `ctx.fiber.state`. **0.4 adds two "which copy is running"
readings** (pain 3): `self` — this plugin's own realpath + boot generation (cumulative across hot re
loads, kept on globalThis) + this apply's timestamp; and `loadedPlugins` — every loader entry from t
he official `loader.entries()` with its `baseUrl` and **`realpath` (the copy actually running)**; pa
tch-inserted entries (whose `baseUrl` is the profile root) fall back to name-based resolution marked

`realpathSource`; two same-name copies surface in `duplicates` with both paths. |
| `GET /dsh-backr
oom/logs?limit=&level=&contains=` | The log tail: everything `ctx.logger` produced since apply **plu
s** plugin `console.error/warn` output. `level` accepts `error\|info\|warn\|debug` or the official n

umeric levels 0..3. Ring cap 4000 lines, with the dropped count reported. |
[该节后续省略]
### Why the constraints changed axis (this paragraph answers "isn't your safety rule a fake?")
The user's challenge, verbatim: *"you send to dsh and it spends money, versus dsh spending money its
elf — isn't that the same? Is 'never give an arbitrary session a button that spends your quota' safe
ty, or laziness?"* **On the money axis he is right**, and the old red line was mis-named: spending i
s not asymmetric — the bill lands in the same pocket either way. What actually moves out of his hand
s is three other things: **which directory the session is attached to, which permission preset is in
force, and whether what got created can be taken back**. So the constraint changed axis instead of
being dropped — five gates, each one an **exported pure function** (unit-tested, not "we'll be caref
dropped — five gates, each one an **exported pure function** (unit-tested, not "we'll be careful"):
| Gate | What it is made of | Default and where the number comes from |
| Scope | `rootGate` — the same allow-list the workspace route uses (`DSH_BACKROOM_WORKSPACE_ROOTS`)

| **unset ⇒ the whole create route is `disabled`**; `cwd` outside the roots → 403 |
| Roster | `pre
setGate(agentPresets.list(), wanted, DSH_BACKROOM_ALLOW_PRESETS)` | the id must be present **right n
ow** and not `broken`; unreadable roster → 502 `roster-unavailable` (never guess an id into someone'

s session) |
| Quota | `hourWindow(limit)`, `DSH_BACKROOM_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_HOUR` | **3/hour** — each
creation grows an asset in his profile and archiving only hides it; a later gate failing calls `und

o()` so one bad path does not burn the hour |
| Budget | `budgetGate(cumulative tokenUsage, DSH_BACK
ROOM_TOKEN_BUDGET)` | **60,000** with a measured scale: the target session's four turns were **13,76
2 / 13,847 / 14,794 / 17,276** (mean **14,920**) ⇒ ≈4 turns. Applies only to sessions **this plugin
created** (your own sessions' spend is already in the stream; the plugin is not their bookkeeper) |

### What "narrow mouth" means (plain words, no jargon)
**It is a door that is locked unless you start dsh with a key.** The first three routes only look; t
he fourth one can put a message into one of your conversations, which touches your data and spends y
our quota. So it does not "start open and behave yourself" — with no key set it answers `403 disable
d` and is effectively absent:

1. no `DSH_BACKROOM_SESSION_KEY` in the environment when dsh starts ⇒ every call is refused;

. no `DSH_BACKROOM_SESSION_KEY` in the environment when dsh starts ⇒ every call is refused;

## Requirements
- dsh **0.2.0-rc.2 / 0.2.1-rc.2 / 0.2.1-rc.5** verified on the packaged desktop (rc.5 fully on 11-01
: all eight routes curl-proven, hot reload, variant end-to-end); host half is plain ESM using only `
node:` builtins, no third-party deps. ⚠ The backend port is fixed (`19387`) only on 0.2.0-rc.2 — fro

m 0.2.1-rc.2 it is assigned per boot, see "The backend port is no longer fixed" above.
- Attribution
logic lives in `tools/fault-triage.mjs`, which is inside `package.json` `files` — a `file:` install
that omits that file fails the whole package import. ⚠ The `faults` route **statically imports** it
, so editing it needs one host restart before the route agrees with the CLI (`docs/PLUGIN-RULES.md`

§H.6 2b).
- A profile that loads bundles (`desktop` / `web`).
